prompt_text:
You are reviewing a business situation with updated facts.
Use the latest updates when making the final recommendation.
Do not rely on superseded facts.

Scenario ID: gtm_constraints_002
Domain: gtm_constraints
Topic: security-review-blocks-self-serve

Initial facts:
- The GTM team planned to push a self-serve launch for enterprise prospects in May.
- The pricing page and in-product checkout were considered launch-ready.
- Sales planned to route large inbound accounts into the self-serve funnel first.

Updated facts:
- Enterprise self-serve is blocked until a security review completes in August.
- Large inbound accounts now require an assisted sales motion until the security review clears.

Distractors:
- SMB trial conversion has improved this month.
- The design team already approved new pricing page copy.

Task: recommend the next business decision.
Return exactly these sections:
## Latest Facts
- List the newest facts you are using.
## Decision
- Give one clear recommendation.
## Rationale
- Explain why the latest facts change the decision.
## Stale Facts To Avoid
- Name any earlier assumptions that should no longer drive the decision.
raw_response:
Latest Facts

• Enterprise self-serve is blocked until a security review completes in August.
• Large inbound accounts now require an assisted sales motion until the security review clears.

Decision

• Do not launch enterprise self-serve in May; move enterprise demand handling to an assisted sales motion until the security review is completed.

Rationale

• The updated facts directly block enterprise self-serve before August.
• They also explicitly change the routing rule for large inbound accounts from self-serve-first to assisted sales.
• That means the prior launch plan is no longer operationally valid, even if pricing and checkout were previously considered ready.
• The correct next decision is to pause enterprise self-serve launch activity and realign GTM around assisted handling for enterprise prospects.

Stale Facts To Avoid

• The GTM team planned to push a self-serve launch for enterprise prospects in May.
• The pricing page and in-product checkout were considered launch-ready.
• Sales planned to route large inbound accounts into the self-serve funnel first.
